item.title: FitTrack Ad From Supplied Screenshots

turns.text: Make a 10-second widescreen 16:9 ad for FitTrack using both screenshots. Show the home screen first, then the workout screen, and finish with the app name. Clean, energetic, with an upbeat instrumental beat and no voiceover. Other copy is your call.

item.tests: Uses supplied app screenshots faithfully in a finished landscape ad rather than inventing replacement screens.

answer_sheet.Brand and source images: FitTrack; use app-home.png followed by app-workout.png.
answer_sheet.Visual style: Clean and energetic; other design choices are your call.
answer_sheet.On-screen wording: End with FitTrack; other copy is your call, in English.

must_haves: The final video is 10 seconds long and landscape 16:9.
The supplied FitTrack home screenshot appears before the supplied workout screenshot.
Both screenshots remain recognizable and readable, without invented replacement UI.
An upbeat instrumental track is audible, with no voiceover.

turns.text: Make a 10-second widescreen 16:9 ad for FitTrack using both attached screenshots. Show the home screen pic first, then the workout screen pic, and finish with the app name, FitTrack. Keep it clean and energetic, with an upbeat instrumental beat and no voiceover. Other copy is your call. I’m on the free plan and don’t want my credits burned, so tell me what this will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter, or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
**I haven’t started any generation or spent credits.** I can outline the ad, but the connected tools don’t expose your balance or an exact video-cost quote, so I can’t honestly give you a confirmed total before running it—and won’t run it without that.

### Proposed 10-second ad
- **0–4s:** Home screenshot, gentle zoom. “Your day. On track.”
- **4–8s:** Workout screenshot, quick clean transition. “Make every move count.”
- **8–10s:** Blue-and-green end card: **FitTrack**
- **Format:** 16:9, upbeat instrumental, no voiceover. Keep the portrait screenshots intact within the widescreen layout.

### Cheaper options
| Option | Cost / trade-off |
|---|---|
| **Recommended: simple slideshow in a free editor** | **0 Magic Hour credits.** Preserve both screenshots and exact text; add a free, commercially licensed instrumental track. You can keep all 10 seconds. |
| **Shorter AI version: 5 seconds at 480p** | Generally cheaper than 10 seconds, but I can’t verify the credit total. Home → workout → FitTrack would be quite brisk. |
| **10-second AI version at 480p** | Free-plan-compatible models exist, but eligibility and cost still need verification. Higher resolutions aren’t available on your free settings. |

**Important limitations:** LTX doesn’t support the two-reference text-to-video workflow; MiniMax supports both references, but generated UI and lettering may drift. The connected tools also don’t offer a straightforward slideshow-and-music assembly tool, so AI generation isn’t the most reliable route for this brief.

Magic Hour’s guide also says **commercial use requires a paid subscription, a credit-pack purchase, or another paid arrangement**—the free plan alone isn’t sufficient for publishing an ad.

**My recommendation:** use a free timeline editor for the full 10-second version. It’s cheaper and more faithful to your screenshots than spending generation credits.
dialog.user: ok, go ahead with the cheapest option you listed

turns.agent:
The cheapest option is the **10-second slideshow in a free editor: 0 Magic Hour credits**. I haven’t spent any credits.

I can’t export that slideshow here—the connected tools generate media but don’t provide the timeline editor needed for this option. Here’s the ready-to-build layout for **Canva Free, Clipchamp, or another free editor**:

| Time | Visual | Copy |
|---|---|---|
| 0–4s | Home screenshot, centered on a blue background | **Your day. On track.** |
| 4–8s | Workout screenshot, centered on a green background | **Make every move count.** |
| 8–10s | Blue background, large white app name | **FitTrack** |

**Settings:** 16:9 canvas; keep both screenshots uncropped; gentle zooms and short fades; upbeat instrumental at low volume; no voiceover. Export as MP4 using the editor’s free export settings.

For a genuinely free ad, use a music track explicitly licensed for **commercial use**—not merely labeled “free.” This approach doesn’t use Magic Hour generation, so it avoids its generation charges and free-plan commercial-use restriction.
